title: 「one 作泛指人稱代名詞」
titleEn: Using “one” as a generic personal pronoun

source.file: Sentence Structure 226 -「one 作泛指人稱代名詞」.pdf
omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no complete English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.
The source filename is numbered 226; it is assigned system ID ss227 because the source set contains two distinct PDFs labelled 201.

formulas.formula: One + singular verb / modal verb + other information
When / If / Before / After / Although + one + singular verb + main clause

example: In an unfamiliar situation, one should remain calm and ask questions.
exampleZh: 在陌生的情況下，人應該保持冷靜並提出問題。

examples.en: In an unfamiliar situation, one should remain calm and ask questions.
examples.zh: 在陌生的情況下，人應該保持冷靜並提出問題。
examples.highlight: In an unfamiliar situation, one should remain calm and ask questions.

meaning.zh: One 可以泛指任何人或一般人，適合用來表達普遍原則、建議、觀察和意見，而不直接以 you 稱呼讀者。

rules.zh: One 後面使用單數動詞。應使用：one is、one has、one does、one needs、one thinks。不要使用：one are、one have、one do、one need、one think。
rules.en: One takes a singular verb: one is, one has, one does, one needs and one thinks.

rules.zh: 人應該仔細檢查自己的成果。） The apostrophe is required: one’s work Do not write: ones work
rules.en: Use one’s for possession and include the apostrophe: “One should check one’s work carefully.”

rules.zh: 人應該容許自己休息。） Do not use themselves when the same person has already been referred to as one in this exercise.
rules.en: Use oneself as the reflexive form. Do not switch to themselves when the same generic person has already been called one.

rules.zh: 人應該保護自己的密碼。） Avoid: One should protect your password. One should protect their password. When one refers to the same person throughout the sentence, use one, one’s and oneself consistently.
rules.en: Keep pronouns consistent: use one, one’s and oneself throughout a reference instead of switching to your or their.

rules.zh: One 的語氣較正式。泛指的 one 特別適合用於作文、報告、正式建議、學術討論、一般原則及經過仔細撰寫的論點。日常對話通常使用泛指的 you 較自然：You never know what will happen。使用 one 的版本較正式：One never knows what will happen。One 並不一定比 you 更好，應按情境和語氣選擇。
rules.en: Generic one is relatively formal and is especially useful in essays, reports, formal advice, academic discussion and carefully written arguments. Generic you is often more natural in ordinary conversation.

rules.zh: One 不一定要放在句首。例子：One should consider the risks. Before one decides, one should consider the risks. I believe that one should consider the risks. Experience can teach one to consider the risks. It is important for one to consider the risks. One 的位置會按照句子結構而改變。
rules.en: One can appear in different sentence positions: at the beginning, inside a dependent clause, after that, as an object, or after a preposition.

rules.zh: 在陌生的情況下，人應該保持冷靜並提出問題。）
rules.en: This exercise uses one to mean any person or people in general. It excludes the number one, one as a replacement for a countable noun, one of + plural noun, and the replacement pronoun ones.

benefits.zh: 可以用來說明任何人都可能遇到的情況，或一般人應該採取的做法。句子的意思不只限於某 一個人。
benefits.en: It helps you express a general principle that applies to any person rather than one named individual.

benefits.zh: 使用 you 有時會令人覺得你正在直接指示讀者。使用 one 則可以把相同意思表達成普遍的觀察 或原則。 Compare: You should check your sources before publishing a claim. （你在發表說法前，應該核實自己的資料來源。） One should check one’s sources before publishing a claim. （人在發表說法前，應該核實自己的資料來源。） The first sentence speaks directly to the reader. The second presents a general rule. 第一句直接向讀者說話；第二句則提出一項普遍原則。
benefits.en: It avoids speaking directly to the reader and presents advice as a general observation or principle.

benefits.zh: 在作文、報告和正式解釋中，如需討論行為、責任、決定或共同經歷，one 十分實用。
benefits.en: It is useful in formal discussion about behaviour, responsibility, decisions and common experiences.

benefits.zh: 和 oneself 可以清楚表示相關物件或動作屬於同一個由 one 所代表的人。 One should accept responsibility for one’s decisions. （人應該為自己的決定承擔責任。） One should give oneself time to improve. （人應該給自己時間進步。）
benefits.en: One’s and oneself keep the reference clear by linking possession or reflexive action to the same generic person.

benefits.zh: 如果多個句子都以 People 或 You 開始，你有時可以使用 one，令句式更有變化。
benefits.en: It gives you an alternative to repeated uses of people and you and creates controlled sentence variety.

benefits.zh: 可以出現在句首、時間或條件子句內、that 之後，或作為動詞及介詞的受詞。這種靈活性有 助你以不同方式組織正式句子。
benefits.en: It can appear in several parts of a sentence, helping you organise formal writing in different ways.
